instructions.title: Instructions for Claude
instructions.lede: What Claude is told about this world before it writes for it through the MCP server: the setting first, then what each kind of thing should be like. Only Claude reads these.
instructions.setting_hint: Which world this is and when: its lands, cities, peoples, factions, gods, tone — and how its races and creatures map onto 5e.
instructions.setting_example: This world is Azeroth from World of Warcraft, at the time of the original game. Use its zones, cities and people (Stormwind, Goldshire, Elwynn Forest, Westfall …). Races: Draenei are Aasimar, Night Elves Wood Elves, Tauren Firbolgs. Monsters unknown to 5e are reskins of book creatures: Murlocs are Kuo-toa, Defias are Bandits.
instructions.adventure_hint: Length, tone, structure, what to avoid.
instructions.adventure_example: Two sessions; one clear villain; a choice that changes the ending; no world-ending stakes.
instructions.chapter_hint: How chapters are written and laid out.
instructions.chapter_example: Each chapter opens with a read-aloud box; secrets in a secret box; at most one fight per chapter.
instructions.npc_hint: Names, factions, how they speak; known figures of the setting and the statblocks they use.
instructions.npc_example: Every NPC has a faction (Alliance, Horde, neutral). Known figures keep their lore: Hogger is a Gnoll Pack Lord, Marshal Dughan a Knight.
instructions.encounter_hint: Difficulty, mix, terrain; which book creatures stand in for the setting's own (shown under their own name).
instructions.encounter_example: Medium or hard; always some terrain to use. Show book creatures under their WoW names (Murloc for Kuo-toa).
instructions.treasure_example: Modest coin; one magic item per adventure at most; trade goods of the region.
instructions.place_hint: Which places to use and how to describe them.
instructions.place_example: Prefer places of the setting's map; describe sound and smell, not only looks.
instructions.saved: Saved — Claude reads them the next time it works in this world.

naming.title: Names
naming.lede: How names are built, by race and culture. Copy a starter, write your own or let Claude research one, and judge thirty samples.
naming.reject_hint: Reject what does not fit: that name is never offered again in this style.
naming.form_lede: The pattern says which parts a name has, each part what it is made of.
naming.raw_lede: The style as JSON, for pasting or for what the form does not reach (documentation/NAMES.md).
naming.name: Name
naming.pattern_hint: {{given}} {{family}}: a part in braces; {{given:initial}} is its first letter.
naming.parts_hint: One entry per line or separated by commas. Fill in the blank row to add a part.
naming.aliases_hint: Comma-separated, such as the books' Dwarf for Zwerg. A character or NPC of that name then finds this style, before the books' tables, in every world.
naming.more_rows: Showing {shown} of {total}. Narrow the search to see the rest.
naming.sources_hint: Where this comes from, one per line. Web addresses become links.
naming.no_style: No style for {race} yet: this is the default.
naming.npc_hint: Race and culture choose the naming style for this NPC. With none that fits, the books' default is used.
naming.drafts_hint: These make no names until you accept them.
naming.draft_note: Claude proposed this style. It is offered nowhere until you accept it.
naming.learned_hint: Paste at least 10 names: new ones are built that sound alike. 2 letters of memory invent more, 3 stay closer to the examples.
naming.kin_hint: Reads that part of a chosen parent's name; with no parent, or none Paravent made, uses the other part of this style.
naming.error.fallback: The part {part} needs another part of this style to fall back to, and it cannot be a parent's name too.
naming.error.learned_few: The part {part} needs at least {count} examples in each list it uses.
naming.error.not_draft: That style is not a draft, so it cannot be replaced.
naming.sounds_hint: Groups: C = k t th r, a capital and its sounds, one group per line. Templates: CV CVC, each capital a sound from its group. A sound listed twice comes up twice as often.
naming.banned_hint: One per line or separated by commas: no name may contain them.
naming.max_cluster: Consonants in a row, at most
naming.max_cluster_hint: Refuses what cannot be said, and three of one letter. Empty checks nothing; 3 suits most languages.
naming.check.runs_out: Only {count} different names came out: the style is small, or its checks refuse most of what it makes.
naming.check.alike: {count} of these start with {letter}: a table will mix them up.
naming.check.none: No names came out: the checks refuse everything this style makes.
naming.error.number: {value} is not a number from {low} to {high}.
naming.error.group: A sound group is a capital, =, and its sounds: {line}
naming.error.syllables: In {part}, the fewest syllables exceed the most.
naming.error.empty_group: In {part}, the group {group} has no sounds.
naming.error.no_group: In {part}, a template uses {group}, but there is no such group.
naming.rewrites_hint: One per line, for what joining breaks: bjornsson = bjarnarson
naming.delete_lede: The style and its rejected names go. Names already given stay.
naming.error.name: A style needs a name.
naming.error.pattern: The pattern names no part. Write parts in braces: {{given}}.
naming.error.unknown_part: The pattern names {part}, but there is no such part.
naming.error.modifier: The pattern uses {modifier}; only initial exists.
naming.error.empty_part: The part {part} has nothing to make a name from.
naming.error.part_key: "{part}" cannot name a part: letters, digits and _ only.
chargen.error.name_style: No name could be made in this world's style.
naming.summary.old-norse: Two elements, then the father's name in the genitive with son or daughter.
naming.summary.old-english: One name of two elements, with no family name.
naming.summary.castilian: A given name, the father's surname, then the mother's.
naming.summary.nahua-calendar: A number and a day sign of the 260-day calendar, as in Ce Acatl, One Reed.
naming.summary.tamil: A given name led by an initial from the father's name, with no family name.
naming.summary.arabic-nasab: A given name, then ibn or bint and the father's name.

npcgen.apply_hint: A ticked name replaces the NPC's name; ticked details are added to the notes.
creatures.heading: Creatures
creatures.lede: Your own creatures: start blank at a challenge rating or from a printed one, check the CR it plays at, and publish it as homebrew.
creatures.empty_text: Start one below, blank or from a creature in your books.
creatures.name: Name
creatures.start_from_hint: A creature as Name|SOURCE, e.g. Bugbear|MM. Its numbers that follow its scores are linked, so they scale.

creatures.published_n.one: Published: {count} creature is in the compendium as Homebrew.
creatures.published_n.other: Published: {count} creatures are in the compendium as Homebrew.

creatures.homebrew_added: Homebrew was added to the books of: {worlds}.
creatures.fit_hint: "Fit to CR" sets AC and hit dice to the Dungeon Master's Guide's values for the chosen CR. The proficiency bonus always follows the CR, and with it every linked attack and DC.
creatures.damage_hint: Comma-separated damage types, e.g. fire, poison.
creatures.ready_made_hint: Traits and actions from the Monster Manual and the Dungeon Master's Guide, with their numbers linked to this creature.
creatures.features_hint: The Dungeon Master's Guide's features that change the CR; # marks those that take a number (dice of extra damage, uses per day).
creatures.dpr_override_hint: Leave empty to read it from the actions. Fill it in for damage the text does not show, such as spells.
creatures.publish_hint: Publish writes every creature to the homebrew file; it then appears in search, on reference pages, in encounters and as NPC statblocks.
creatures.delete_lede: The design is deleted and its statblock leaves the homebrew. Encounters that use it show it as missing.
creatures.not_found_lede: This creature does not exist, or was deleted.
creatures.est_table_values: AC {ac} · HP {hp_min}–{hp_max} · attack {attack} · {dpr_min}–{dpr_max} damage · DC {dc} · proficiency {pb}
creatures.estimate_matches: By the Dungeon Master's Guide's method it plays at the CR you chose.
creatures.estimate_differs: By the Dungeon Master's Guide's method it plays at a different CR. Its statblock keeps the CR you chose; adjust AC, hit dice or damage, or choose that CR.
creatures.note.saves: Several saving throw proficiencies raise its effective AC.
creatures.error.name: A creature needs a name.
creatures.error.name_taken: There is already a creature called {name}.
creatures.error.base: No creature {ref} in the loaded books.

translation.note.stale: Translated from an older version of the English text ({stale} passages)
translation.note.partial: Partly translated ({done} of {total} passages); the rest is in English
translation.note.english: Not translated yet: shown in English
translate.title: Translate {name}
translate.nothing_open: Nothing left to do here: every passage is translated and reviewed.
translate.insert_tag: Insert this tag at the cursor
translate.stale_hint: The English text changed after this was translated
translate.name: Name
translate.machine_hint: Drafts for every untranslated passage, marked until reviewed
translate.confirmed: Every draft is marked as reviewed.
translate.machine_done: Machine drafts added. Review them before relying on them.
translate.error.service: The translation service did not answer. Nothing was changed; try again later.
translations.title: Translations
translations.lede: How much of the rules, creatures, spells and books reads in this language, and what to translate next. Untranslated text shows in English.
translations.machine_off: No translation service is configured. Set PARAVENT_TRANSLATE_API_KEY (a Claude API key) on the server to draft translations by machine.
translations.machine_hint: Drafts every untranslated passage of what you choose, through the Claude API: the English text is sent to Anthropic, and it costs per passage. Drafts are marked until someone reviews them; passages whose tags would change stay English.
translations.started: Machine drafts started. Progress shows below.
translations.job_counts: {passages} passages drafted, {rejected} kept English, {failed} not reached
translations.wanted_hint: The entries the books link to most often that have no translation yet.
translations.wanted_none: Every linked entry has a translation.
translations.problems_hint: The English text changed since these were translated, or a passage they translate no longer exists. They still show; review and save them.
translations.lost_hint: The entry, chapter or book these translate is no longer in the data, or goes by another name, so nothing shows them. Name the entry they belong to now, as Name|SOURCE; the box starts with the likely one. Every passage moves as it is, and what differs from the new English then shows as outdated.
translations.drafts_lede: Translations drafted by machine and not yet read. They show in the language, marked as drafts, until someone confirms them in the editor.

translations.drafts_waiting.one: {count} record holds drafts nobody has confirmed yet.
translations.drafts_waiting.other: {count} records hold drafts nobody has confirmed yet.

translations.drafts_confirm_all.other: Confirm the drafts of all {count} records

translations.drafts_confirm_hint: Marks every draft listed here as reviewed, unread. Each still shows its text; the editor changes it later.
translations.players_job: What players read, all of it
translations.unfinished_lede: Records with passages still in English, most often ones the machine gave back with a link or roll changed, which are never stored. Open one to translate the rest by hand, or let the machine try them again.

translations.unfinished_waiting.one: {count} record is translated only in part.
translations.unfinished_waiting.other: {count} records are translated only in part.

translations.unfinished_retry_hint: Runs in the background on the overview; what comes back with its tags intact is stored as a draft, the rest stays English.
translations.moved: Translation moved. Passages that differ from the new English are listed under Needs a look.
translations.move_unknown: There is no entry "{entry}" to move it to.
translations.move_not_lost: "{entry}" is no longer waiting to be moved.
translations.move_taken: "{entry}" already has a translation. Tick the box to replace it, or choose another entry.
translations.import.title: Import a translated corpus
translations.import.hint: A corpus in another language in the 5eTools format, in a folder on this server (under Docker, a folder mounted into the container). A passage is taken only where its links match the English, and arrives as a draft unless you say otherwise. Your own translations are kept.
translations.import.reviewed: Take as reviewed, not as drafts
translations.import.started: The import runs in the background.
translations.import.done: Imported from {folder}. New passages wait as drafts.
translations.import.nothing: Nothing in {folder} matched the English corpus.
translations.import.misaligned: Chapters not lined up with the English, left out: {books}
translations.import.error.folder: “{entry}” is not a folder on this server.
translations.import.error.own: “{entry}” is the English corpus or Paravent's library; choose the translated corpus.

corpus.title: 5eTools data
corpus.lede: Which 5eTools release this is, and whether Paravent reads every file of it: files that do not parse, entries that fail validation, keys nobody reads, counts that do not add up. Run it after replacing the data. It also holds your own work against the data: translations, names and links.
corpus.references: Also check every reference in the data: entries, descriptions, rulebooks, adventures (a few seconds more)

corpus.vtt_skipped.one: {count} Foundry VTT file skipped, as always: it holds no content.
corpus.vtt_skipped.other: {count} Foundry VTT files skipped, as always: they hold no content.

corpus.subject: About
corpus.no_changes: Nothing changed: the same keys, fields and row counts.
corpus.counts_hint: Rows in the files, less those rejected or repeating another's name and book, plus the magic items made from variants, must equal the entries loaded.
corpus.not_loaded_hint: Keys Paravent knows and does not read yet, and files no loader reads.
corpus.fields_hint: Fields of loaded entries no model declares. They are kept unchanged; no screen uses them yet. A new one after an update is worth a look.
corpus.never_hint: Run a check to see whether every file reads.
corpus.unconfigured_hint: Set PARAVENT_REFERENCE_DIR to the folder of your 5eTools data and restart.
corpus.cli: The same check from the command line:
corpus.kind.unreadable: Files that are not valid JSON
corpus.hint.unreadable: The file was skipped entirely. Usually a truncated download or a hand edit.
corpus.kind.not_object: Files that are not a JSON object
corpus.hint.not_object: 5eTools files hold an object of arrays; this one holds something else and was skipped.
corpus.hint.bad_row: An array of entries holds something that is not an entry; it was skipped.
corpus.hint.invalid: The entry lacks a field Paravent needs or holds one in a shape it cannot read. It is missing from search and from every link to it.
corpus.kind.unresolved_copy: Copies of entries that do not exist
corpus.hint.unresolved_copy: The entry is a patch (_copy) of another entry that was not found, so it was skipped.
corpus.kind.unknown_copy_mode: Patch modes Paravent does not know
corpus.hint.unknown_copy_mode: A _copy patch uses a mode added upstream. The patch was skipped, so the entries using it are subtly wrong.
corpus.hint.missing_template: A creature names a template (bestiary/template.json) that does not exist; it loads without it.
corpus.hint.missing_item_entry: An item's text is a {#itemEntry} reference to shared text in items-base.json that does not exist; the item shows the reference.
corpus.hint.unfilled_item_entry: Shared item text asks the item for a value (a colour, a damage type) it does not have; the gap shows as written.
corpus.kind.count_mismatch: Counts that do not add up
corpus.hint.count_mismatch: The store holds a different number of entries than the files explain — entries were lost or invented somewhere without a report.
corpus.hint.fluff_invalid: A fluff record (description, images) could not be read; its entry shows without it.
corpus.kind.fluff_unresolved: Descriptions copying one that does not exist
corpus.hint.fluff_unresolved: A fluff record copies another that was not found.
corpus.hint.table_unreadable: A table a feature reads (treasure, encounters, names, creature builder) has changed shape upstream.
corpus.hint.unknown_key: New upstream, most likely: nothing reads it, and nothing was planned for it.
corpus.hint.missing_file: The feature that reads this file has nothing to show.
corpus.hint.table_empty: The file was read, but the feature found none of the tables it looks for.
corpus.kind.missing_body: Books and adventures without their text
corpus.hint.missing_body: The index lists it, but its text file is missing; it shows in lists and cannot be opened.
corpus.hint.unindexed_body: A book or adventure text that books.json or adventures.json does not mention cannot be reached.
corpus.kind.lookup_missing: Spell lists naming spells not loaded
corpus.hint.lookup_missing: The spell-list lookup names spells of a book whose spells are not loaded.
corpus.hint.unknown_tag: A tag new upstream: it shows as its plain text until the renderer learns it.
corpus.hint.duplicate_key: Two rows share a name and book; the later one is kept.
corpus.hint.fluff_orphans: Normal in part: some describe creature groups or are only copied from.
corpus.hint.dead_reference: Tags naming an entry no loaded book holds (often a table inside a rulebook or an item group). They show as grey text.
corpus.hint.translation_stale: The English changed since these passages were translated. They still show, marked as outdated; the link opens them beside the new English.
corpus.hint.translation_orphan: The English they translate is gone or moved, so they no longer show. They stay in the file until someone copies them over; the detail names their old place.
corpus.hint.translation_lost: The entry, chapter or book these translate is no longer in the data, or goes by another name. They stay in the file; nothing shows them.
corpus.hint.translation_tags: Tags of the English that the translation lacks: a link or a roll the reader does not get.
corpus.hint.translation_link: Tags in translated text naming an entry no loaded book holds. They show as grey text.
corpus.kind.glossary_lost: Names of entries that are gone
corpus.hint.glossary_lost: Glossary names whose English entry is no longer in the data, or goes by another name. Harmless, but the name no longer shows.
corpus.kind.library_book: Books no longer in the data
corpus.hint.library_book: Books a world or adventure declares, or an adventure is based on. What they held will not resolve.
corpus.hint.library_reference: Encounters, NPCs, treasure, characters, running fights or book chapters naming an entry or section the data no longer holds.
corpus.hint.library_link: Links in chapters, notes and session notes that lead nowhere, found as the chapter check finds them: references, NPCs, chapters, headings, images.

backup.title: Backups
backup.lede: Copies of everything made with Paravent — worlds, adventures, characters, fights, users, homebrew, media, translations. Never the 5eTools data, which you can download again.
backup.off_hint: Set PARAVENT_BACKUP_DIR in .env to a folder outside the library and restart. PARAVENT_BACKUP_AT sets the times of day.
backup.on_demand: Only when started here or from the command line (PARAVENT_BACKUP_AT is empty), keeping the newest {keep}.

check.kind.excluded: In a book this world leaves out:
check.kind.heading: No such heading:

themes.lede: How Paravent looks: its colours, fonts and pictures. Choose one for yourself; the table's theme is what everyone else sees.
themes.follow_table_hint: Whatever the gamemaster chooses for everyone; now {name}.
themes.paravent_hint: Paravent's own look, clear and modern.
themes.install: To install a theme, put its folder into the library:
themes.problem.external: {file} loads from another server; the browser will refuse that part.
themes.problem.icons: icons.svg lacks {count} icons ({names}); Paravent's own are used.
themes.problem.empty: Nothing to draw: no tokens.css, skin.css or complete icons.svg.

naming.world.title: Names in this world
naming.world.lede: The naming styles this world's names are rolled from — for NPCs, characters, the creatures of its encounters and fights, and its places. Nothing ticked: every style.
naming.world.workshop: Styles are made and changed in the workshop:
naming.world.saved: Saved. Names in this world now come from these styles.
naming.world.unserved: No style names these peoples of {world} yet; their names come from a fallback.
naming.world.all_served: Every people of this world's NPCs and characters has a style.

naming.roll_none: No style is made for this creature: the default stands in.
naming.error.roll: No name could be rolled in this style.
